cases.title: claim() never records voucher redemption, allowing unlimited signature replay
cases.status: confirmed by an executable Foundry PoC (test/SignatureVoucherClaimExploit.t.sol, passing)
cases.description: SignatureVoucherClaim.claim() verifies that `signature` is a valid admin signature over `(recipient, amount, voucherId, address(this))`, then immediately pays out `amount` in ETH to `recipient` — but never records, by voucherId or by the signature/digest itself, that this voucher has already been redeemed. The exact same signed voucher therefore remains valid forever and can be submitted to `claim()` an unlimited number of times, each call paying out the full `amount` again, draining the contract far beyond the single payout the admin actually authorized. This is a pure missing-replay-protection bug (no nonce, no used-voucher mapping, no expiry) — the signature verification itself is correct.
cases.source_richness: high — the bug lives in this repo's own 42-line contract, executable PoC included (test/SignatureVoucherClaimExploit.t.sol), exact scenario: an admin signs one voucher authorizing a 1 ETH payout, and the same signature is submitted 4 times, draining 4 ETH from a contract funded with 10 ETH, when only 1 ETH was ever authorized.
